---
title: "Development"
---

Working on captain-hook itself. For using captain-hook in your project, see [Installation](../getting-started/installation.qmd).

## Setup

Clone the repo and sync the dev extra:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yasyf/captain-hook
cd captain-hook
uv sync --extra dev
```

### NLP assets

Tests that exercise NLP signals need the spaCy English model and WordNet data:

```bash
uv run python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
uv run python -c "import wn; wn.download('oewn:2025')"
```

This mirrors what CI provisions — see `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Tests

Run the suite:

```bash
uv run pytest
```

The example hooks in `docs/examples/` carry inline tests too:

```bash
uv run capt-hook --hooks docs/examples test
```

## Docs

The docs are Great Docs (Quarto), published to GitHub Pages. The API reference is generated from docstrings at build time; the CLI reference comes from the Click app.

Sync the docs group alongside the dev extra, then preview locally:

```bash
uv sync --extra dev --group docs
uv run great-docs preview
```

## Build and smoke-test the wheel

Build the wheel, then install and exercise it in a throwaway venv:

```bash
uv build
uv venv --seed .wheel-smoke
uv pip install --python .wheel-smoke/bin/python dist/*.whl
.wheel-smoke/bin/capt-hook --help
```

## Using a local checkout

From a consumer project, point `uv run --project` at your clone:

```bash
uv run --project path/to/captain-hook capt-hook test
```

## Releasing

Bump `version` in `pyproject.toml`, add the CHANGELOG entry, and commit them together with `uv.lock`, which pins the package's own version. Then tag the new version and push. `.github/workflows/release-pypi.yml` builds the sdist and wheel, publishes to PyPI via trusted publishing, and cuts a GitHub release:

```bash
git tag v0.9.1
git push origin v0.9.1
```

The release workflow re-derives the wheel version from the tag via `uv version --frozen`, so tag the same version you bumped to.
